facts.statement: Sankar Chatterjee first announced the discovery of Polarornis gregorii in 1989 but did not officially describe and name the species until 2002.
facts.quote: The discovery of Polarornis gregorii was first announced by Sankar Chatterjee in 1989, but he did not describe and officially name the species until 2002.

facts.statement: The single known species, Polarornis gregorii, was found on Seymour Island, Antarctica, in Late Cretaceous rocks dated to about 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: It contains a single species Polarornis gregorii, known from incomplete remains of one individual found on Seymour Island, Antarctica, in rocks which are dated to the Late Cretaceous (López de Bertodano Formation, about 66 Ma).

facts.statement: Polarornis is classified as a prehistoric bird that is either a possible member of the family Vegaviidae or the group Aequornithes.
facts.quote: Polarornis is a genus of prehistoric bird, either a possible member of the Vegaviidae or Aequornithes.

facts.statement: Gerald Mayr criticized the original description of the fossils, noting that Polarornis differed from loons in important characteristics and that the specimen's completeness was overstated.
facts.quote: Gerald Mayr, for example, noted that Polarornis differed from loons in some important characteristics, and criticized Chatterjee's original description of the fossils for overstating the specimen's completeness.

facts.statement: A 2025 study by Irazoqui and colleagues recovered Polarornis as a member of Aequornithes, with one analysis grouping it with Gaviidae.
facts.quote: In their 2025 description of Pujatopouli, Irazoqui and colleagues recovered Polarornis as a member of the Aequornithes based on the Neornithes dataset, with one analysis grouping it with Gaviidae.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Polarornis is the family Vegaviidae.
Polarornis lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
